messages:
jess: noticing a big uptick in tiny-pod Pending in eu-west1 around 03:10 UTC, warm-pool nodes not absorbing them. lots of small gangs stuck -> fragmentation + evictions. anyone else seeing this?

tom: saw the alert. total pending count ~320, normal ~70. heatmap shows pocketing in a few racks. :eyeglasses:

nikita: digging into scheduler logs — attach/detach timeouts for ENIs spike, then scheduler's packing loop gives up and leaves tiny pods Pending instead of coalescing.

sam: are these pods using strict podAffinity or nodeSelector for GPU flavor? that would prevent packing.

jess: most are `resources: nvidia.com/gpu: 0.125` (fractional gang) + `topologyKey: rack` affinity from batch jobs. also a few have `node.kubernetes.io/fast-network:NoSchedule` taints on warm nodes.

nikita: taint + fractional GPU is a nasty combo — scheduler sees warm nodes as incompatible, falls back to cold nodes and we get striping across racks. leads to tiny leftover slots and fragmentation.

tom: provisional mitigation: relax the taint on a subset of warm nodes for the next 30m to let fractional pods co-locate, then re-taint. low-friction?

sam: that sounds reasonable. we should gate by node egress cost — if we pack more, some pods will end up on warm nodes with higher egress billing. tradeoff: fewer evictions vs higher network unit cost.

jess: agree. cost hit estimated ~5% on eu-west1 egress for the batch window, but evictions are causing sustained retries that inflate CPU/GPU charge way more.

lia-ops-bot: automatic note: warm-pool scaler observed throttling at 03:12 UTC, scaling events suppressed for 90s due to backoff.

nikita: quick commands I ran: `kubectl get pods -n batch -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` showed AttachVolume timeout ~120s. attaching ENI metrics from cloud: `ENIAttachLatency` spike at 03:09.

tom: action plan proposal: 1) temporarily remove `fast-network` taint on 6 warm nodes in eu-west1a, 2) bump warm-pool target by +25% for 20 minutes, 3) run a one-shot descheduler job to coalesce tiny pods onto warmed nodes, 4) monitor eviction rate and egress cost.

sam: +1. add canary: only do 2 nodes first and watch. also set an autoscaler emergency rollback if eviction rate doesn't drop in 10m.

jess: I'm running step 1 now on 2 nodes, tagging `eng-platform` to watch.

nikita: while you're doing that, I'll draft a small scheduler tweak we can test: reduce the packing excellence threshold so fractional-gang coalescing is favored even if it marginally increases network egress score. config snippet: `--priority-function-config=favor-packing:0.12` (conceptual).

tom: remember we can't ship scheduler changes without a canary. do the node untaint first and let the descheduler do the heavy lifting.

lia-ops-bot: deploy-bot: descheduler job `coalesce-tiny-gangs-eu-west1` queued, will run in 2 minutes.

jess: seeing Pending drop from 320 -> 180 after untaint on 2 nodes. eviction spikes down too. :thumbsup:

sam: good sign. if this holds for 15m we can proceed with +25% warm target. please log the egress delta for billing.

nikita: noted — I pulled a quick cost delta estimate, pushing to the incident doc: https://confluence.internal/infra/eu-west1-frag-2026 (private).

jess: final-ish: we'll re-taint the nodes after 30m and run a cleanup job to rebalance. file follow-ups in #postmortems if anything weird shows up. thanks all.
